category-weighted-grade.formula: category% = earned/possible*100; overall = sum(category% * weight) / sum(weight). Letter bands A >= 90, B >= 80, C >= 70, D >= 60.
category-weighted-grade.edition: Pure weighted-mean arithmetic; standard US letter bands, by name; the instructor's gradebook governs.
category-weighted-grade.freeAccess: Pure public algebra; bands vary by school.
category-weighted-grade.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
category-weighted-grade.editionNote: Normalizing by the sum of weights handles a partially-complete term; a category with possible = 0 is excluded.

assumptions.name: Letter bands
assumptions.value: A >= 90, B >= 80, C >= 70, D >= 60 (standard US)

wip-percent-complete.formula: pct = min(cost_to_date / est_total_cost, 1); earned = pct x contract; over_under = earned - billed.
wip-percent-complete.edition: The cost-to-cost percent-of-completion revenue recognition and the over/under-billing schedule from construction accounting (ASC 606 / AICPA construction guide), by name.
wip-percent-complete.freeAccess: Cost-to-cost percent-of-completion and the WIP over/under-billing schedule are standard published construction-accounting methods.
wip-percent-complete.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
wip-percent-complete.editionNote: The cost-to-cost percent-of-completion (POC) method: percent complete = cost to date / estimated total cost (capped at 100%), earned revenue = percent complete x contract value, and over/under billing = earned revenue - billed to date. A positive result is underbilled (a costs-and-estimated-earnings-in-excess-of-billings asset); a negative result is overbilled (a billings-in-excess liability, cash collected against work not yet done). This is a management snapshot from the entered figures; it does not adjust for unapproved change orders, and the CPA-prepared WIP schedule and the estimate's accuracy govern.

assumptions.name: Percent complete
assumptions.value: cost to date / estimated total cost, capped at 100%

assumptions.name: Over/under billing
assumptions.value: earned revenue - billed to date (+ underbilled asset, - overbilled liability)

assumptions.name: Estimate-driven
assumptions.value: accuracy depends on the estimated total cost; the CPA WIP schedule governs

search-probability.formula: cumulative_POD = 1 - product(1 - POD_i); POS = POA * cumulative_POD; residual = POA * (1 - cumulative_POD).
search-probability.edition: Standard SAR search theory (Koopman detection theory) as used in the U.S. National SAR Supplement and NASAR / FEMA search-planning doctrine, by name.
search-probability.freeAccess: POD/POA/POS definitions are public; method cited, not reproduced.
search-probability.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
search-probability.editionNote: Assumes independent passes - correlated searches overstate cumulative POD. POS is always <= POA.

assumptions.name: Independence
assumptions.value: passes treated as statistically independent; correlated passes overstate cumulative POD

conductivity-from-tds.formula: conductivity_us_cm = tds_mgl / k_factor; k commonly 0.55-0.75 (default 0.65); band EC = TDS/0.75 to TDS/0.55.
conductivity-from-tds.edition: Electrical conductivity from total dissolved solids (Standard Methods 2510), the inverse of the TDS estimate, by name.
conductivity-from-tds.freeAccess: The TDS = k x EC correlation is a standard published water-quality relation; the k factor is calibrated to the specific water.
conductivity-from-tds.governance: Estimate. Operator of record and primacy agency govern.
conductivity-from-tds.editionNote: Electrical conductivity from total dissolved solids, the inverse of the TDS-from-conductivity estimate: EC (uS/cm at 25 C) = TDS (mg/L) / k, with the correlation factor k commonly 0.55-0.75 (default 0.65) depending on the dominant dissolved ions. Because a fixed TDS maps to a range of conductivity as k varies, the band EC = TDS/0.75 to TDS/0.55 is reported so the number is not read as exact. This is useful to predict a conductivity-meter reading from a target or permit TDS, or to set an EC alarm setpoint. The result is an estimate, not a measurement; calibrate k against a paired laboratory TDS and EC for the specific source water. An operations aid; the operator of record and the primacy agency govern compliance.

assumptions.name: Correlation
assumptions.value: EC (uS/cm at 25 C) = TDS (mg/L) / k

assumptions.name: Factor range
assumptions.value: k commonly 0.55-0.75 by ion makeup; default 0.65

assumptions.name: Estimate
assumptions.value: not a measurement; calibrate k to a paired lab TDS and EC

wire-ampacity.formula: A steady-state thermal balance (I^2 R heating against convective and radiative surface loss) with the coefficient calibrated to a 75 C THWN #12 in 30 C ambient, times the NEC 310.15(C)(1) adjustment for more than 3 current-carrying conductors. NOT a Table 310.16 lookup; it reads high above about 8 AWG.
wire-ampacity.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
wire-ampacity.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow NEC 2023. NEC 2026 is the current published edition; jurisdictions on NEC 2017 / 2020 / 2023 / 2026 use slightly different ambient corrections and ampacity ranges; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ.

assumptions.name: Termination temperature
assumptions.source: NEC 110.14(C) default for the typical residential / light-commercial install

assumptions.name: Ambient temperature
assumptions.value: 30°C unless user supplies

assumptions.name: Current-carrying conductors per raceway
assumptions.value: ≤ 3 unless user supplies

co-air-free.formula: CO_air_free = measured_co_ppm x 20.9 / (20.9 - measured_o2_pct); over_ansi = CO_air_free > 400; over_field = CO_air_free > 100.
co-air-free.edition: ANSI Z21 400 ppm air-free limit / BPI field practice air-free CO correction, by name.
co-air-free.freeAccess: The air-free CO correction is standard combustion-analysis practice; the analyzer and appliance manufacturer instructions govern the actual screening.
co-air-free.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
co-air-free.editionNote: As-measured CO is diluted by excess and dilution air and reads deceptively low, so a dangerous appliance can look acceptable. The sample must be taken in the flue, before the draft hood or dilution air, or the correction over-inflates. The correction scales the reading to a no-dilution basis for comparison to the air-free limit: 400 ppm air-free (ANSI Z21), under 100 ppm field target. The analyzer and the manufacturer instructions govern - a safety-screening aid, not a certified combustion test.

assumptions.name: Air-free basis
assumptions.value: the ANSI Z21 400 ppm CO limit is air-free; measured CO must be corrected up to it

assumptions.name: Sample point
assumptions.value: sample in the flue, before the draft hood or dilution air, or the correction over-inflates

hydraulic-cylinder.edition: First-principles fluid power; NFPA T2.13.7 (hydraulic cylinder dimensions / definitions) by name.
hydraulic-cylinder.freeAccess: Free at nfpa.com for the NFPA fluid-power table of contents.

nfpa-1142-water-supply.formula: WS = (V * CCN) / OHC per NFPA 1142 Ch. 4 (Occupancy Hazard Classification Number OHC 3-7 divides; Construction Classification Number CCN 0.5-1.5). 1.5x exposure multiplier when adjacent structure within 50 ft. 0.5x sprinkler reduction when UL-listed system present.
nfpa-1142-water-supply.edition: NFPA 1142-2022 (Standard on Water Supplies for Suburban and Rural Firefighting) Ch. 4.

power-triangle.formula: kVA^2 = kW^2 + kVAR^2; PF = kW / kVA; theta = arccos(PF). Any two of kW / kVA / kVAR / PF / angle fix the triangle, provided at least one is a magnitude.
power-triangle.edition: IEEE 1459 (Definitions for the Measurement of Electric Power Quantities). Sinusoidal-case algebra.
power-triangle.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
power-triangle.editionNote: Single-edition (IEEE 1459 power-quantity definitions; the sinusoidal-case power triangle is a physical identity).

assumptions.name: Sinusoidal system
assumptions.value: the classic power triangle applies to sinusoidal voltage and current; non-sinusoidal systems add a distortion-power term

assumptions.name: Reactive sign
assumptions.value: lagging (inductive) reactive power is drawn by motors and shown positive (IEEE 1459); leading (capacitive) by over-correction, shown negative

water-heater-input.formula: input BTU/hr = (recovery_gph × 8.33 × delta-T) / recovery efficiency; electric kW = input / 3412. The inverse of gph = (input × efficiency) / (8.33 × delta-T).
water-heater-input.edition: DOE 10 CFR 430 water-heater efficiency test procedure; AHRI 1300 (residential water heaters).
water-heater-input.freeAccess: Free at energy.gov/eere for DOE test procedures and ahri.org for the AHRI directory / TOC.
water-heater-input.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed plumber / gas fitter govern. Verify against the IPC / IFGC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
water-heater-input.editionNote: The burner or element input a water heater needs to sustain a target recovery rate, the inverse of water-heater-recovery: input = recovery_gph × 8.33 × rise / efficiency, and for an electric heater the kW output is the input divided by 3412 BTU/hr per kW. This is the steady recovery input; the AHRI first-hour rating also credits the stored tank volume, so a tank can meet a short peak with less input than this. Recovery-efficiency defaults (0.98 electric / 0.80 atmospheric gas / 0.94 condensing gas) are test-procedure conventions; the nameplate governs. AHJ governs.

assumptions.name: Recovery efficiency
assumptions.value: 0.98 electric / 0.80 atmospheric gas / 0.94 condensing gas unless the user enters the nameplate value

assumptions.name: Steady recovery only
assumptions.value: sizes the steady input; the first-hour rating credits stored volume, so a tank meets short peaks with less input

assumptions.name: Water energy constant
assumptions.value: 8.33 BTU per gallon per degree F

defensible-space.formula: (reference page; no compute) Zone 0 / 1 / 2 wildland-urban-interface defensible-space actions per CALFIRE 2022 guidance and NFPA 1140 (Standard for Wildland Fire Protection, 2022), which absorbed NFPA 1144 (Reducing Structure Ignition Hazards from Wildland Fire).
defensible-space.edition: CALFIRE 2022 'Defensible Space' guidance by name; NFPA 1140 (formerly 1144) by name. IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home program by name.
defensible-space.freeAccess: CALFIRE guidance free at readyforwildfire.org. NFPA 1140: Free read-only access at nfpa.org/freeaccess. IBHS guides free at ibhs.org.
defensible-space.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed fire protection engineer govern.
defensible-space.editionNote: Editions available: CALFIRE 2022 (Zone 0 / Ember-Resistant Zone added 2020), NFPA 1140-2022 (NFPA 1144 was withdrawn into it; there is no 1144-2023). Verify the current edition adopted by your state forestry agency / AHJ.

excavation.formula: Volume = D × (L × W + (L + W) × s + 4 s² / 3), the prismoidal volume of a pit with a constant side slope (setback s = D / tan(angle) per side), for OSHA-compliant slopes (Type A / B / C per OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P).
excavation.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed structural engineer govern.

assumptions.name: Soil swell factor
assumptions.value: user-supplied; typical 25% for clay / 15% for sand

as-purchased-quantity.formula: ap_quantity = ep_quantity_needed / (yield_pct / 100); ap_units = unit_weight > 0 ? ap_quantity / unit_weight : n/a.
as-purchased-quantity.edition: As-purchased quantity from edible-portion needed (standard culinary math; CIA The Professional Chef; Labensky, On Cooking; ServSafe), by name; the actual yield varies with grade, season, and trimming, so a yield test on the real product governs.
as-purchased-quantity.freeAccess: The as-purchased-quantity relation is public culinary math (the inverse of yield); the edible-portion amount needed, the yield percentage, and the purchase-unit weight are the kitchen's values.
as-purchased-quantity.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
as-purchased-quantity.editionNote: Kitchens buy ingredients as-purchased -- whole, untrimmed, bone-in -- but serve them as edible portions, and the two weights differ because trimming, peeling, boning, and cooking loss all remove weight. The yield percentage is the fraction of the as-purchased weight that survives to the plate. This calculation answers the purchasing question, which is the inverse of the more familiar yield calculation that starts from a known as-purchased weight: to find how much to buy for a needed edible-portion amount, you divide the edible-portion quantity by the yield expressed as a fraction. Because the yield is always less than one, dividing by it always produces a purchase quantity larger than what will be served, and the lower the yield the larger the gap -- a 50% yield doubles the amount that must be bought. To plate 20 pounds of trimmed beef tenderloin at a 75% yield, the kitchen must purchase 20 divided by 0.75, or 26.67 pounds; to end up with 10 pounds of diced onion at an 88% yield takes 10 divided by 0.88, or 11.36 pounds as purchased. When the ingredient is bought in a fixed unit -- a case, a bag, or an each of known weight -- dividing the as-purchased quantity by that unit weight gives the number of units to order, which in practice is rounded up. This is a purchasing estimate; the true yield of any given product varies with its grade, the season, and how aggressively the cook trims, so a yield test performed on the actual product governs the order.

assumptions.name: AP from EP
assumptions.value: AP = EP needed / yield (always divide, so the buy exceeds what is served); AP units = AP / unit weight, rounded up
assumptions.source: CIA / On Cooking / ServSafe culinary math

assumptions.name: Yield varies
assumptions.value: the real yield changes with grade, season, and trimming; a yield test on the actual product governs the order

thaw-time.formula: thaw_time_hr = (density_pcf x latent_heat_btu_lb / (cooler_temp_f - thaw_point_f)) x (P x a_ft / h_coeff + R x a_ft^2 / k_unfrozen); thaw_time_days = thaw_time_hr / 24.
thaw-time.edition: Plank's equation applied to thawing, with the ASHRAE Handbook Refrigeration shape constants cited by name and not reproduced, reported against the four thawing methods permitted by FDA Food Code section 3-501.13, cited by section; the Food Code method and a measured product temperature govern.
thaw-time.freeAccess: The conduction relation is public physics and the Food Code methods are cited by section, not mirrored. The product's dimension, density, latent heat, thaw point, cooler temperature, and conductivities are the user's values.
thaw-time.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
thaw-time.editionNote: Thawing is Plank's equation run in the other direction and two things change, both pushing the same way. The driving temperature difference is now the cooler above the product's thaw point rather than the freezer below it, and a 38 F walk-in against a 28 F thaw point gives about 10 degrees where a blast freezer at -10 F gave nearly 40. The internal conduction now happens through the thawed outer layer, whose thermal conductivity is roughly a third of the frozen product's. Together they make thawing take several times longer than freezing did, which is the fact kitchens most often get wrong. The reversal shows up in the two terms: on a frozen slab the surface term usually dominates and airflow is the lever, while in thawing the internal term usually exceeds it, so thickness controls and blowing more air at a frozen turkey does very little. The estimate brackets the familiar USDA rule of roughly 24 hours of refrigerator thawing per four to five pounds a little long, which is the safe direction. The FDA Food Code permits four thawing methods and countertop thawing is not among them; the tile names them so the number lands with its rule.

assumptions.name: Unfrozen conductivity
assumptions.value: conduction is through the THAWED outer layer, whose k is roughly a third of the frozen value

assumptions.name: Permitted methods
assumptions.value: FDA Food Code section 3-501.13: refrigeration at 41 F or below; running water at 70 F or below reaching 41 F within four hours; microwave immediately followed by cooking; or as part of cooking

assumptions.name: Cross-check
assumptions.value: USDA rule of thumb, roughly 24 hours of refrigerator thawing per 4 to 5 pounds
assumptions.source: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service

drying-times.formula: (reference page; no compute) Typical drying-time benchmarks for common building materials (drywall 2-4 days, hardwood 5-10+ days, carpet pad 1-2 days, plaster 5-14 days, framing 3-7 days, concrete varies) based on engineering-practice observations and original plain-English notes.
drying-times.edition: IICRC S500-2021 by name; original plain-English notes by the project author.
drying-times.freeAccess: IICRC standards licensed; engineering-practice observations free in published restoration training literature.
drying-times.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.

crop-yield.formula: Adjusted yield = field_yield × (1 − moisture_field) / (1 − moisture_standard). Standard moisture: corn 15.5%, soybean 13.0%, wheat 13.5% (USDA standard).
crop-yield.edition: USDA Federal Grain Inspection Service (FGIS) standard moisture grades by name.
crop-yield.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.

assumptions.name: Standard moisture
assumptions.value: corn 15.5% / soy 13.0% / wheat 13.5%

cardioid-sub-array.formula: c = 49.03 x sqrt(temp_f + 459.67), about 1,128 ft/s at 70 F; delay_per_element_ms = spacing_ft / c x 1000; optimum_freq_hz = c / (4 x spacing_ft); wavelength_ft = c / optimum_freq_hz; spacing_for_target_ft = c / (4 x target_freq_hz).
cardioid-sub-array.edition: End-fire and reverse-stack cardioid subwoofer arrays from the quarter-wavelength spacing relation, by name; standard live-sound system design practice built on public acoustics. A measurement system and the room govern the deployed result.
cardioid-sub-array.freeAccess: The quarter-wave rear-cancellation geometry is public acoustics; the spacing, element count, and temperature are the designer's own values.
cardioid-sub-array.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
cardioid-sub-array.editionNote: An end-fire array puts subwoofers in a line pointed at the audience and delays each one behind the one in front by exactly the time sound takes to travel the spacing. Forward, every cabinet's output arrives together and adds. Backward, the electronic delay and the acoustic travel time add rather than cancel, so the rear arrivals are spread out in time and the level collapses. The rejection is deepest where the spacing is a quarter wavelength, because that puts the rear arrivals a half wavelength -- a full polarity flip -- apart, which places the optimum at the speed of sound divided by four times the spacing. That quarter-wave relationship is the whole design and it also sets the usable band: an array tuned for deep rejection at one frequency is progressively less directional below it, and above roughly twice the tuning frequency the pattern breaks up. Adding elements deepens and broadens the rejection but does not move where it is centered, so the only way to tune lower is to open the spacing, which costs stage depth in direct proportion. That trade -- depth of stage against depth of rejection -- is the real constraint on end-fire arrays, and it is why a low-tuned array is often impossible on a shallow deck. The reverse-stack cardioid variant, one cabinet turned to face backward and delayed with its polarity inverted, works on the same arithmetic with the spacing set by the cabinet depth rather than chosen.

assumptions.name: Quarter-wave spacing
assumptions.value: deepest rejection where the spacing is one quarter wavelength, putting rear arrivals a half wavelength apart

assumptions.name: Usable band
assumptions.value: less directional below the tuning frequency; the pattern breaks up above roughly twice it

assumptions.name: Element count
assumptions.value: more elements deepen and broaden the rejection but do not move its center frequency

cap-rate-dscr.formula: Cap rate = NOI / property_value (as a percent). DSCR = NOI / annual_debt_service. NOI is gross income minus operating expenses (excluding debt service, depreciation, income tax). Bands are common-practice; not agency-defined.
cap-rate-dscr.edition: Standard CRE underwriting ratios. Universal in commercial-real-estate practice.
cap-rate-dscr.freeAccess: Public reference; covered in every introductory CRE finance text.

assumptions.name: NOI scope
assumptions.value: gross income minus operating expenses; EXCLUDES debt service, depreciation, income tax

assumptions.name: Cap-rate bands
assumptions.value: <4 prime, 4-6 strong, 6-8 typical, >8 higher-risk

lighting-beam.formula: Beam (pool) diameter = 2 x throw x tan(beam angle / 2); center illuminance E = candela / distance^2 (inverse-square). Candela from lumens = lumens / (2*pi*(1 - cos(beam angle / 2))). 1 fc = 10.764 lux.
lighting-beam.edition: First-principles theatrical photometry - beam spread and the inverse-square illuminance the form fixture photometric charts (manufacturer cut sheets) publish, by name; public domain.
lighting-beam.freeAccess: Public first-principles photometry. The center-beam candela / field-vs-beam angle come from the fixture's photometric data; a real beam is brighter at center than the edge.
lighting-beam.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
lighting-beam.editionNote: Single-edition (physics). Point-source / single-fixture model; for room or area average illuminance (lumen method) use the lux-to-footcandle tile. The lumens-to-candela conversion is an average-over-the-cone estimate.

assumptions.name: Point source
assumptions.value: single aimed fixture, inverse-square from the photometric center; no field falloff or atmospheric loss modeled

water-extraction-rate.formula: standing = area x (depth_in / 12) x 7.48052; absorbed = area x gal per sq ft; total = the sum; wand time = total / effective gpm; dumps = ceil(total / tank gal); weight = total x 8.3454; dehumidification days = total / gal per day.
water-extraction-rate.edition: Standing volume from area and depth at 7.48052 gallons per cubic foot, absorbed water from an assembly absorption rate, and water weight at 8.3454 lb per gallon, by name; the extraction-versus-evaporation comparison uses a real-world daily dehumidifier removal that is entered rather than assumed. Volume, time, and logistics only. ANSI/IICRC S500, the local sewer authority, and the restorer's own moisture readings govern.
water-extraction-rate.freeAccess: Volume arithmetic on the user's own measurements and rates; no equipment performance table is reproduced.
water-extraction-rate.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
water-extraction-rate.editionNote: The first rule of water damage restoration is that every gallon extracted is a gallon the dehumidifiers never have to evaporate, and the arithmetic makes the point brutally rather than rhetorically: a wand pulling several gallons a minute does in an afternoon what a large dehumidifier at a real-world daily rate would take more than a month to do. Extraction is not a preliminary step, it is the step, and everything the drying equipment does afterward is the small remainder. Two sources of water behave differently and both belong in the number. Standing water is a straight volume calculation and comes up fast. Absorbed water is held in the carpet, the pad, and the substrate, it comes up slowly, and it is what decides whether a second and third pass is worth making -- which it almost always is, because the marginal gallon from a slow pass is still hundreds of times cheaper than evaporating it. The two logistics outputs are what actually plan the day: wand time sets the labor, and the waste-tank dump count sets how many trips to the drain the crew makes, which on a large loss is a scheduling constraint rather than a detail. The effective extraction rate is the input to be careful with, because it is not the pump's rated flow -- it depends on the wand, the operator, the substrate, and how much of each pass is spent moving rather than pulling, and it falls sharply as the material dries, which is exactly why later passes take longer for less water.

assumptions.name: Extraction beats evaporation
assumptions.value: by two to three orders of magnitude; every extracted gallon is one the dehumidifiers skip

assumptions.name: Effective rate is not rated flow
assumptions.value: it depends on wand, operator, and substrate, and it falls as the material dries

assumptions.name: Category 2 and 3 water is regulated
assumptions.value: extracted water is contaminated and its disposal requires the sewer authority's approval

plating-tank-current.formula: total current = current density x area; mass rate g/s = I x atomic weight / (valence x 96,485) x current efficiency; volume rate = mass rate / density; thickness rate = volume rate / area in cm2; time = target thickness / thickness rate.
plating-tank-current.edition: Faraday's law of electrolysis, mass rate = current x atomic weight / (valence x 96,485 C/mol) x current efficiency, by name, with deposit thickness following from the metal's density and the part's surface area. AVERAGE thickness only. The bath supplier's data, the plating specification, and the applicable environmental and safety regulations govern.
plating-tank-current.freeAccess: Faraday's law and the Faraday constant are public physics; the metal's atomic weight, valence, and density are published constants and the current efficiency is entered by the user.
plating-tank-current.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
plating-tank-current.editionNote: Plating and anodizing are the one shop process governed by an exact physical law. Faraday's law says the mass deposited is exactly proportional to the charge passed, with the constant of proportionality being the metal's equivalent weight over the Faraday constant, and nothing about the bath chemistry, the additives, or the operator changes that. What they change is current efficiency, the fraction of the current that deposits metal rather than evolving hydrogen -- nickel baths run near ninety-five percent while decorative chromium baths run in the teens, which is the whole reason chrome plating is so slow and so power-hungry. The useful reading is that current density, not total current, sets the rate. A part twice as large needs twice the current to plate in the same time, and a rectifier that cannot deliver it simply plates slower, so doubling the rack area without doubling the rectifier halves the current density and doubles the time. Current density also has upper and lower limits set by the bath, because too low gives poor coverage and too high burns the deposit, so the practical rate is bounded by chemistry rather than by the power supply. The one thing to hold onto is that this is an average thickness and an inspector measures a local one. Current concentrates at edges and points and starves in recesses, so a rack that averages the target may be well over on a corner and well under in a bore, and throwing power, anode placement, robbers, and shields are the entire craft of fixing that. The same law run in the other direction, on metal being consumed rather than deposited, is the sacrificial-anode life calculation.

assumptions.name: Faraday's law is exact
assumptions.value: mass is exactly proportional to charge; only the current efficiency varies

assumptions.name: Current density sets the rate
assumptions.value: not total current -- a larger rack on the same rectifier simply plates slower

assumptions.name: Average, not local
assumptions.value: edges run heavy and recesses thin; throwing power and shielding govern uniformity

porta-wrap-friction.formula: hold(n) = load x exp(-mu x n x 2 pi) for n = 1..4 wraps (capstan / Euler-Eytelwein equation). More wraps, exponentially less hand force.
porta-wrap-friction.edition: Capstan (Euler-Eytelwein) friction equation and ANSI Z133-2017 by name; first-principles mechanics.
porta-wrap-friction.freeAccess: The capstan equation is public physics. ANSI Z133-2017 is a published consensus standard.
porta-wrap-friction.governance: Math aid for personal verification. Stop work and consult the qualified person on site if any number does not match the field condition.
porta-wrap-friction.editionNote: More wraps means less hand force but a harder, slower release and more heat - too many can lock and shock the system on a moving piece. The load side is the piece's dynamic tension under control, not just its static weight, so pair with tree-rigging-shock. A groundie keeps hands clear of the device and never wraps a hand in the tail.

assumptions.name: Friction coefficient
assumptions.value: rope-on-device ~0.20 (default; depends on device, rope, glaze, moisture)

bar-nesting.formula: usable = stock - end trim; pieces sorted descending; first-fit-decreasing places each piece in the first stick where used + length + (kerf if the stick is not empty) <= usable, opening a new stick otherwise; total kerf = sum over sticks of (pieces on that stick - 1) x kerf; drop = total stock - part - kerf - trim; yield = part / total stock; lower bound = ceil((total part + (pieces - sticks) x kerf) / usable).
bar-nesting.edition: One-dimensional cutting-stock, packed by the first-fit-decreasing heuristic - a standard, near-optimal bin-packing method, not a proprietary nesting algorithm.
bar-nesting.freeAccess: First-fit-decreasing is textbook combinatorial optimization; nothing here is licensed or tabulated.
bar-nesting.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
bar-nesting.editionNote: Why longest-first: the long pieces have the least flexibility, so placing them while every stick is still empty leaves the short pieces to fill the gaps they leave behind. Reversing the order strands long pieces on sticks that short ones have already nibbled, and the stick count goes up. The kerf accounting is the detail hand estimates miss - kerf is charged per CUT, not per piece, so a stick holding n pieces takes n-1 kerfs, and a stick that happens to cut clean to its end takes one fewer than a stick with drop left over. The worked example makes that concrete: three 62s, a 38, and a 14.5 come to 238.5 in of part plus four 0.125 in kerfs, exactly filling the 239 in usable length with ZERO drop. Honesty about the method: first-fit-decreasing is a heuristic, not an optimum. The tile computes a material lower bound alongside its answer and states plainly whether the packing has reached it - when it has, no rearrangement saves a stick; when it has not, a hand rearrangement or a true cutting-stock solver may do better. Not modeled: clamping and chuck loss, grain or finish direction, mill tolerance on the stock length, reusable drop carried in from an earlier job, or nesting across more than one stock size. The longest single drop is reported precisely so it can be checked against the next cut list before it goes in the rack. Verify the pattern against the saw setup before cutting. A material-ordering aid; the cut list and the shop govern.

assumptions.name: Heuristic
assumptions.value: first-fit-decreasing; near-optimal but not guaranteed optimal

assumptions.name: Kerf accounting
assumptions.value: charged per cut, so n pieces on a stick take n-1 kerfs

assumptions.name: End trim
assumptions.value: deducted from every stick before packing

assumptions.name: Lower bound
assumptions.value: material-based; reported so the user knows whether the packing can be beaten

assumptions.name: Not modeled
assumptions.value: clamping loss, grain direction, stock tolerance, reusable drop, multiple stock sizes

assumptions.name: Size limit
assumptions.value: 5,000 pieces, to keep the packing responsive in the browser

vessel-head-volume.formula: 2:1 semi-elliptical head V = pi D^3 / 24; hemispherical V = pi D^3 / 12; ASME flanged-and-dished (torispherical) V ~ 0.0810 D^3; straight flange V = pi/4 D^2 x length; gallons = in^3 / 231.
vessel-head-volume.edition: Dished-head volume geometry, first-principles; the inside diameter, head type, and straight-flange length come from the head. The ASME F&D figure is a standard-geometry approximation.
vessel-head-volume.freeAccess: The elliptical and hemispherical head volumes are exact first-principles solids of revolution; the F&D approximation and the head dimensions come from the head maker's stamp.
vessel-head-volume.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
vessel-head-volume.editionNote: The bulge volume of one dished tank head past its tangent line. A 2:1 semi-elliptical head (depth D/4) is a half-ellipsoid, V = pi D^3 / 24; a hemispherical head (depth D/2) is a half-sphere, V = pi D^3 / 12; a standard ASME flanged-and-dished (torispherical) head is close to 0.0810 D^3 for the common crown = D, knuckle = 0.06 D geometry -- this is an approximation and the exact volume needs the actual crown and knuckle radii. Add the straight-flange (cylindrical skirt) section pi/4 D^2 x length. Two heads give a tank's end allowance on top of the straight-shell volume; the head manufacturer's stamped dimensions govern.

assumptions.name: Head geometry
assumptions.value: elliptical = half-ellipsoid (pi D^3/24), hemispherical = half-sphere (pi D^3/12), both exact

assumptions.name: F&D approximation
assumptions.value: standard flanged-and-dished ~ 0.0810 D^3; the actual crown and knuckle radii shift it

cctv-storage.formula: Per camera per day GB = bitrate_Mbps * 0.45 * recording_hours (1 Mbps for 24 h = 10.8 GB/day); total = cameras * per-camera-day * retention_days; aggregate bandwidth = cameras * bitrate.
cctv-storage.edition: IP-video storage and bandwidth from bitrate, recording hours, and retention (1 Mbps for 24 h is about 10.8 GB/day), per the standard NVR/VMS sizing practice; first-principles bitrate accounting.
cctv-storage.freeAccess: First-principles bitrate accounting. The H.264/H.265 bitrate estimates are scene- and vendor-specific and user-supplied; the VMS calculator and the installed cameras govern.
cctv-storage.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
cctv-storage.editionNote: First-principles (no edition). A motion duty-cycle scales the recording hours; a retention of 0 days yields 0 storage rather than an error.

assumptions.name: Bitrate
assumptions.value: per-camera bitrate is user-supplied or estimated from resolution/fps/codec

pool-cya-dose.formula: Raise: ~0.81 lb (~13 oz) cyanuric acid per 10,000 gal per 10 ppm; lower: drained fraction = 1 - target/current.
pool-cya-dose.freeAccess: Product labels and SDS free with the chemical; CPO course materials proprietary.
pool-cya-dose.governance: Math aid for personal verification. Stop work and consult the qualified person on site if any number does not match the field condition.
pool-cya-dose.editionNote: Single-edition (engineering-practice / first-principles take-off; refresh as practice and product data shift).

assumptions.name: Target CYA band
assumptions.value: ~30-50 ppm outdoor chlorine pool (advisory)

control-joint-spacing.formula: Spacing = min(factor x thickness, cap); depth = 0.25 x thickness; panels = ceil(length/spacing) x ceil(width/spacing); aspect kept under ~1.5:1.
control-joint-spacing.freeAccess: ACI documents licensed; the rule of thumb is public practice.
control-joint-spacing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
control-joint-spacing.editionNote: Single-edition (engineering-practice / first-principles take-off; refresh as practice and product data shift).

assumptions.name: Spacing factor and cap
assumptions.value: ~2.5 ft per inch of thickness, capped ~15-18 ft (editable)

circulating-load-ratio.formula: U/O = (o - f)/(f - u) on one size class (f classifier feed, o overflow, u underflow, percent); circulating load % = 100 U/O; underflow = (U/O) x new feed; classifier feed = new feed + underflow.
circulating-load-ratio.edition: The two-product formula for a classifier closing a grinding circuit, a steady-state mass balance on one size class (as in Wills' Mineral Processing Technology), by name.
circulating-load-ratio.freeAccess: A mass balance on the user's own size assays; no published data is bundled.
circulating-load-ratio.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
circulating-load-ratio.editionNote: Steady-state circulating load from a single size class, dry solids basis; the classifier overflow equals the new feed. The result is sensitive to assay error when the feed fraction is close to either product, so use the size class with the widest spread or average several. A screen; a full mass balance governs.

assumptions.name: Two-product formula
assumptions.value: U/O = (o - f)/(f - u)

assumptions.name: Steady state
assumptions.value: overflow = new feed; no accumulation in the mill or sump

well-shock-chlorination.formula: well_volume_gal = 0.0408 x casing_in^2 x column_ft; bleach_gal = volume x target_ppm / (1,000,000 x (bleach% / 100)); available_cl_lb = (volume / 1,000,000) x target_ppm x 8.34.
well-shock-chlorination.edition: AWWA A100 / state private-well shock-chlorination guidance (by name).
well-shock-chlorination.freeAccess: State and extension well-disinfection guides are public; bleach strength is on the label.
well-shock-chlorination.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
well-shock-chlorination.editionNote: Single-edition (the local health department and state well code govern the procedure).

assumptions.name: Target concentration
assumptions.value: default 100 ppm; a shock is commonly about 50 to 200 ppm held overnight (often 12 to 24 hours)

assumptions.name: Bleach strength
assumptions.value: plain unscented household bleach, about 5 to 8.25% available chlorine; ignores the slight bleach specific gravity, so round up

assumptions.name: Clearance
assumptions.value: pump to waste until the chlorine clears, then retest; the health department governs the bacteriological clearance

three-point-bridle.formula: Li = sqrt(e^2 + n^2 + rise^2); ui = (e, n, rise)/Li; T1 u1 + T2 u2 + T3 u3 = (0, 0, W) solved by Cramer's rule; angle_i = asin(rise_i / Li).
three-point-bridle.edition: Entertainment rigging three-point bridle geometry (static 3-D resolution), by name.
three-point-bridle.freeAccess: Static bridle resolution is a public statics result; ASME B30.9 governs rigging practice. An ESTIMATE only; the hardware ratings and a qualified rigger govern.
three-point-bridle.governance: Estimate. Head rigger and manufacturer working-load-limit charts govern. Inspect every piece of hardware before the show.
three-point-bridle.editionNote: The solution is physical only while every leg tension is positive (a rope can only pull - the apex must hang horizontally inside the triangle of its attachment points); an asymmetric hang splits the load far from evenly (the near, steep legs carry most of it); the in-plane two-leg case is bridle-leg-tension. A design aid, not a rigging sign-off.

assumptions.name: Three-dimensional statics
assumptions.value: single apex, three straight legs to fixed points, load acts straight down; ropes carry tension only

assumptions.name: Estimate only
assumptions.value: the hardware working load limits and a qualified rigger govern the actual pick

wire-rope-clips.formula: clip_count from OSHA Table H-2 by rope diameter (1/2 & 5/8 -> 3, 3/4 & 7/8 -> 4, 1 -> 5, 1-1/8 & 1-1/4 -> 6, 1-3/8 & 1-1/2 -> 7; below 1/2 -> 2 per manufacturer); spacing_in = 6 x rope_diameter_in.
wire-rope-clips.edition: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.251 Table H-2 (formerly Table H-20) wire-rope U-bolt clip requirements, by name; the clip and rope manufacturer and OSHA govern the termination.
wire-rope-clips.freeAccess: The clip count and spacing are in OSHA 29 CFR 1926.251 Table H-2 (public federal regulation); the U-bolt orientation and torque come from the clip manufacturer.
wire-rope-clips.governance: Estimate. Head rigger and manufacturer working-load-limit charts govern. Inspect every piece of hardware before the show.
wire-rope-clips.editionNote: The minimum number and spacing of U-bolt wire-rope clips to form a load-bearing eye, from OSHA 29 CFR 1926.251 Table H-2 (the old H-20). The clip count steps with the rope diameter (1/2 and 5/8 in take 3 clips, 3/4 and 7/8 in take 4, 1 in takes 5, up to 7 for 1-3/8 and 1-1/2 in), and the clips are spaced 6 times the rope diameter on center. The U-bolt (the threaded saddle) MUST bear on the DEAD (short) end of the rope and the clip base on the LIVE (load-bearing) end -- 'never saddle a dead horse' -- and the nuts are torqued to the manufacturer's value in sequence and RE-torqued after the rope has been loaded once. OSHA does not tabulate below 1/2 in; 2 clips is the common manufacturer minimum there. A correctly installed U-bolt clip eye develops only about 80% of the rope's breaking strength (a swaged or poured socket is stronger). This counts and spaces the clips; the clip and rope manufacturer's instructions, the required torque, and OSHA govern the actual termination, and a qualified person inspects it.

assumptions.name: Clip count and spacing
assumptions.value: OSHA Table H-2 count by diameter; spacing = 6 x rope diameter on center

assumptions.name: Saddle on the live end
assumptions.value: U-bolt on the dead end, base on the live end; torque per the maker and retorque after first load

insulation-resistance-pi.formula: dar = IR(60 s) / IR(30 s); polarization_index = IR(10 min) / IR(1 min). IEEE 43 bands: PI < 1 dangerous, 1-2 questionable, 2-4 good, > 4 excellent; DAR < 1.25 marginal, 1.4+ good.
insulation-resistance-pi.edition: IEEE 43 (Recommended Practice for Testing Insulation Resistance of Electric Machinery) polarization index and dielectric absorption ratio, by name; the machine baseline trend and the OEM acceptance criteria govern.
insulation-resistance-pi.freeAccess: The PI and DAR are public ratios of timed insulation-resistance readings; the interpretation bands are the IEEE 43 guidance, and the readings come from the megger test.
insulation-resistance-pi.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
insulation-resistance-pi.editionNote: A timed insulation-resistance (megger) test reveals winding condition through how the measured resistance changes over time, not just its absolute value. When test voltage is applied, clean dry insulation keeps absorbing (polarizing) charge, so its apparent resistance keeps climbing for many minutes; wet, dirty, or cracked insulation stops climbing or falls as leakage current dominates. Two ratios capture that: the dielectric absorption ratio DAR = IR at 60 seconds / IR at 30 seconds (a quick 1-minute test), and the polarization index PI = IR at 10 minutes / IR at 1 minute (note the 1-minute and 60-second readings are one and the same). By IEEE 43, a PI below 1.0 is dangerous and warrants investigation, 1.0-2.0 is questionable, 2.0-4.0 is good, and above 4.0 excellent; a DAR below about 1.25 is marginal and 1.4 or above is good. This is a TREND and SCREEN, not a stand-alone pass/fail: the readings must be temperature-corrected to a common base (insulation resistance roughly halves for each 10 C rise) before they are compared against a machine's own history, and IEEE 43 cautions that on modern high-resistance epoxy-mica windings that already read above about 5,000 Mohm at one minute, the PI loses diagnostic meaning and the absolute IR and its trend govern instead. The machine's baseline trend, the OEM's acceptance criteria, and the test standards (IEEE 43 / 95) govern the verdict.

assumptions.name: PI and DAR ratios
assumptions.value: DAR = IR(60s)/IR(30s); PI = IR(10min)/IR(1min); rising IR = good insulation; IEEE 43 interpretation bands

assumptions.name: Trend, not pass/fail
assumptions.value: temperature-correct to a common base (~halve IR per 10 C); PI loses meaning above ~5000 Mohm at 1 min; the baseline trend and OEM criteria govern

steel-h1-interaction.formula: ratio = Pr/Pc; ratio >= 0.2: I = Pr/Pc + (8/9)(Mrx/Mcx + Mry/Mcy); ratio < 0.2: I = Pr/(2Pc) + (Mrx/Mcx + Mry/Mcy); pass when I <= 1.0.
steel-h1-interaction.edition: The AISC 360-22 Section H1.1 combined-force (axial plus flexure) bilinear interaction equations, consistent for ASD or LRFD, by name.
steel-h1-interaction.freeAccess: AISC 360 is free to read at aisc.org (Specification for Structural Steel Buildings); the H1.1 interaction equations are in the published specification.
steel-h1-interaction.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
steel-h1-interaction.editionNote: The AISC 360-22 H1.1 combined-force equations - Pr/Pc + (8/9)(Mrx/Mcx + Mry/Mcy) for Pr/Pc >= 0.2 and Pr/(2Pc) + (Mrx/Mcx + Mry/Mcy) for Pr/Pc < 0.2 - consistent for ASD (available = nominal/Omega) or LRFD (available = phi x nominal). This evaluates the H1.1 interaction from the required and available strengths supplied - it takes Pc and Mc as already computed (from steel-column-capacity and steel-beam-ltb in the same ASD or LRFD basis), assumes the second-order (P-delta/P-Delta) amplification is already in Mr (Chapter C / Appendix 8), and does not cover the H1.3 out-of-plane or H2 unsymmetric-member cases. A design aid, not a substitute for the structural engineer of record's stamped design.

assumptions.name: Bilinear interaction
assumptions.value: the 8/9 form for Pr/Pc >= 0.2, the half-axial form below, capped at 1.0

assumptions.name: Available strengths
assumptions.value: Pc and Mc entered from the member tiles in a consistent ASD or LRFD basis

assumptions.name: Second-order
assumptions.value: the P-delta/P-Delta amplification is already carried in the required moment Mr

velocity-head.edition: The velocity-head and dynamic-pressure relations from first-principles fluid mechanics, by name.
velocity-head.freeAccess: Velocity head and dynamic pressure are standard fluid-mechanics relations. The code velocity limits and the engineer of record govern.
velocity-head.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
velocity-head.editionNote: Velocity head h_v = V^2 / (2g) is the kinetic energy of the flow expressed as feet of fluid, and the dynamic pressure q = 1/2 rho V^2 is that energy as a pressure. Both scale with the square of velocity, so doubling the velocity quadruples the head and pressure - the reason a small velocity increase drives large minor (fitting) losses and erosion, and why plumbing codes cap water velocity around 5-8 ft/s. This returns the head and dynamic pressure for the entered velocity and fluid density (water default rho 1.94 slug/ft^3): it does not itself compute the friction or minor losses. A design aid; the code velocity limits and the engineer of record govern.

assumptions.name: Dynamic pressure
assumptions.value: q = 1/2 rho V^2; water rho 1.94 slug/ft^3

assumptions.name: V-squared law
assumptions.value: both scale with V^2; a small velocity rise drives large minor losses

drip-edge-takeoff.formula: slope factor = sqrt(1 + (rise/12)^2); rake LF = rake count x plan run x slope factor; eave LF = plan eave length; pieces = ceil(LF x (1 + waste) / (stock - lap/12)).
drip-edge-takeoff.edition: Roof takeoff geometry - no standard claimed; the eave-under / rake-over installation convention is manufacturer installation guidance.
drip-edge-takeoff.freeAccess: Geometry; drip-edge installation direction is published in every manufacturer's instructions.
drip-edge-takeoff.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
drip-edge-takeoff.editionNote: RAKES RUN UP THE SLOPE AND EAVES DO NOT - that is the whole reason to split them, and it is what a single perimeter number silently loses: a 6:12 rake measured off the plan under-orders by about 12%, an 8:12 by 20%. The second reason to separate them is that the profiles differ and install opposite ways relative to the underlayment - eave drip goes UNDER so water leaving the shingles is carried past the fascia, rake drip goes OVER - and reversing either is a leak. Pieces are figured on an effective stick length of stock minus the lap, since every joint consumes that lap. Valley metal, step flashing at walls (step-flashing-count), and the starter course are separate items, and hips and ridges carry no drip edge at all. The roofing plan and the manufacturer's installation instructions govern.

assumptions.name: Slope factor on rakes only
assumptions.value: rakes take sqrt(1 + (rise/12)^2); eaves are horizontal and take plan length

assumptions.name: Effective stick length
assumptions.value: stock length minus the lap at each joint

assumptions.name: Profiles differ
assumptions.value: eave drip installs under the underlayment, rake drip over; counted separately

shear-flow-connector-spacing.formula: Q = A y_bar (first moment of the connected element about the neutral axis); q = V Q / I (shear flow); s = n R / q (max connector spacing).
shear-flow-connector-spacing.edition: First-principles mechanics of materials (shear flow in a built-up beam), as in Hibbeler Mechanics of Materials and Gere; the connector capacity R is from AISC and entered.
shear-flow-connector-spacing.freeAccess: The shear-flow relation q = VQ/I and the connector-spacing s = nR/q are standard published mechanics-of-materials results (Hibbeler, Gere, Roark), reproduced in every strength-of-materials text.
shear-flow-connector-spacing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
shear-flow-connector-spacing.editionNote: The horizontal shear flow at a connected interface of a built-up beam and the connector spacing that carries it. q = V Q / I, where V is the transverse shear at the section, I is the moment of inertia of the WHOLE built-up section about its neutral axis, and Q = A y_bar is the first moment of the CONNECTED element (the area on one side of the interface) about that neutral axis. The connectors carry q per inch, so the maximum spacing is s = n R / q with R the capacity of one connector and n the connectors per row. The spacing tightens where the shear is largest (near supports); a fabricator often steps the bolt pattern along the shear diagram. First-principles mechanics; the connector capacity R (bolt shear, weld strength) comes from AISC and is entered here. A design aid, not a substitute for the engineer of record.

assumptions.name: Shear flow
assumptions.value: q = V Q / I, Q = A y_bar of the connected element about the section neutral axis

assumptions.name: Connector spacing
assumptions.value: s = n R / q; the connector capacity R is entered (from AISC bolt/weld strength)

spt-required-n60.formula: N60 = qa_target / qa(N60=1), the Meyerhof SPT allowable qa = [N60/4 (B <= 4 ft) or (N60/6)((B+1)/B)^2] x Kd solved for the blow count; Kd = min(1 + 0.33 D/B, 1.33).
spt-required-n60.edition: The Meyerhof (1956) SPT settlement-based allowable bearing on sand (N60/4 and (N60/6)((B+1)/B)^2 ksf; Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering, 8th ed., Eqs. 7.32-7.33, which carry no depth factor), solved for the blow count, with the depth factor Kd = 1 + 0.33 D/B (capped at 1.33) applied as in spt-bearing-capacity. Das prints that depth factor only with Bowles' (1977) modified form, N60/2.5 and N60/4 (Eqs. 7.34-7.35), which runs about 50% higher; this tile keeps the conservative original constants.
spt-required-n60.freeAccess: The Meyerhof N-value allowable-bearing correlations are standard published foundation-engineering results.
spt-required-n60.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
spt-required-n60.editionNote: The inverse of spt-bearing-capacity: the energy-corrected SPT N60 the sand must show to carry a target allowable pressure at a 1 inch settlement. Because qa is linear in N60 (both footing branches) and the depth factor Kd is independent of N60, the required N60 is the target pressure divided by the allowable at N60 = 1; round up to the next whole blow count for design. This is a settlement-controlled (serviceability) check against the boring's N-value, not the ultimate bearing capacity; N60 must be energy-corrected, and a high water table near the footing roughly halves the capacity (raising the required N60) and is not applied here. A design aid; the engineer of record and the geotechnical report govern.

assumptions.name: Blow count from pressure
assumptions.value: N60 = qa_target / qa(N60=1), qa linear in N60 in both branches

assumptions.name: Depth factor
assumptions.value: Kd = min(1 + 0.33 D/B, 1.33), independent of N60

assumptions.name: Settlement-controlled
assumptions.value: 1 in settlement check; N60 energy-corrected; round up for design

snowmelt-load.formula: q_o = q_s + q_m + A_r(q_h + q_e), with q_s = 2.6 s (32 - t_a); q_m = 746 s; q_h = 11.4 (0.0201 V + 0.055)(33 - t_a); q_e = 1075.5 (0.0201 V + 0.055)(0.188 - p_av); p_av from the Magnus curve x RH; boiler = q_o x area x (1 + back_loss); t_m ~ 0.5 q_o + 33.
snowmelt-load.edition: ASHRAE Handbook (HVAC Applications, Snow Melting and Freeze Protection) steady-state surface flux, with the Chapman (1956) IP component forms as printed in Lund, Pavement Snow Melting (Geo-Heat Center / OSTI), by name.
snowmelt-load.freeAccess: The energy balance is stated in the ASHRAE snow-melting chapter and the Chapman closed forms are reproduced verbatim in Lund's Geo-Heat Center paper (free via OSTI); the Magnus saturation curve and steam-table h_fg are public; the arithmetic is public.
snowmelt-load.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
snowmelt-load.editionNote: ASHRAE snow-melting steady-state surface flux q_o = q_s + q_m + A_r(q_h + q_e): warm the falling snow to 32 F (q_s = 2.6 s (32 - t_a), s in in/hr water equivalent), melt it (q_m = 746 s), and over the snow-free fraction A_r pay the exposed wet surface's convective (q_h = 11.4 (0.0201 V + 0.055)(33 - t_a), V in mph) and evaporative (q_e = h_fg (0.0201 V + 0.055)(0.188 - p_av), p_av in in Hg) losses -- the Chapman (1956) IP forms as printed in Lund, with h_fg = 1075.5 Btu/lb at the film (a steam-table value; Lund leaves it symbolic) and 0.188 in Hg the saturation pressure at the film. The ambient vapor pressure comes from the August-Roche-Magnus saturation curve times the relative humidity. A_r is Chapman's class choice: 0 Class I (residential, may run snow-covered), 0.5 Class II (commercial), 1.0 Class III (critical; must stay clear). The boiler output adds the ~20% ASHRAE-typical back-and-edge loss for an insulated slab (bridges and exposed backs run higher), and the mean fluid temperature is roughly 0.5 q_o + 33 F (Chapman's rule of thumb). A steady-state design flux for the chosen storm, not an annual energy; the idling/pickup strategy, controls, and glycol fluid design follow the manufacturer's manual. A sizing aid, not a stamped hydronic design.

assumptions.name: Energy balance
assumptions.value: q_o = q_s + q_m + A_r(q_h + q_e) at the 33 F melting film

assumptions.name: Class ratio
assumptions.value: A_r = 0 / 0.5 / 1.0 for Class I / II / III; the class, not the climate, is the first sizing question

assumptions.name: Back loss
assumptions.value: boiler = q_o x area x (1 + ~20%) for an insulated slab back; exposed backs run higher

desiccant-airflow-sizing.formula: lb_per_hr = required_pints_per_day x 1.043 / 24; process_cfm = lb_per_hr x 7000 / (4.5 x design_grain_depression); units_needed = ceil(process_cfm / nameplate_process_cfm). 4.5 = 60 min/hr x 0.075 lb/ft^3 standard air; 7000 grains/lb; 1.043 lb/pint.
desiccant-airflow-sizing.edition: Psychrometric mass balance and the desiccant process-airflow method, by name; ANSI/IICRC S500. The 4.5 / 7000 / 1.043 constants are not edition-bound.
desiccant-airflow-sizing.freeAccess: The same psychrometric mass balance the grains-removed tile uses, in reverse: process airflow carries the water-removal rate across the wheel at the design depression.
desiccant-airflow-sizing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
desiccant-airflow-sizing.editionNote: Single-edition (the mass balance and the constants do not roll). The manufacturer's performance map, reactivation exhaust ducting, and chamber conditions GOVERN the achievable grain depression - this is a sizing screen, and desiccant reactivation air must be ducted outside. ANSI/IICRC S500 names the deep-drying method.

assumptions.name: Standard air
assumptions.value: 4.5 lb/hr per cfm per (grains/lb/7000) = 60 min/hr x 0.075 lb/ft^3 standard air density

assumptions.name: Constants
assumptions.value: 7000 grains/lb, 1.043 lb/pint water density

assumptions.name: Achievable depression
assumptions.value: the manufacturer's performance map governs the inlet->outlet grain depression; reactivation exhaust air must duct outside

pipe-filled-support-load.formula: empty_lbft = (pi/4)(OD^2 - ID^2)/144 x pipe_density; fluid_lbft = (pi/4)(ID^2)/144 x fluid_density; insul_lbft = (pi/4)((OD + 2 thk)^2 - OD^2)/144 x insul_density; filled = empty + fluid + insul; per_hanger = filled x spacing.
pipe-filled-support-load.edition: First-principles cross-section x density; the MSS SP-58 operating support load the result feeds, by name. Not edition-bound.
pipe-filled-support-load.freeAccess: The support load is a pure cross-section-times-density buildup; the standard pipe weights and water density are public.
pipe-filled-support-load.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
pipe-filled-support-load.editionNote: Single-edition (the geometry does not roll). Pipe weight is computed from the entered OD, wall and steel density (no weight table is bundled; MSS SP-58 / hanger-maker charts are the cross-check) and the water density is taken at 62.4 lb/ft^3 - a hot or dense fluid changes the contents weight, and concentrated loads (valves, flanges) are added separately. MSS SP-58 names the operating support load this feeds.

assumptions.name: Pipe weight
assumptions.value: computed from the entered OD/wall and material density (steel 490, copper 558 lb/ft^3); nominal mill values

assumptions.name: Water density
assumptions.value: contents taken at 62.4 lb/ft^3 unless a different fluid density is entered

assumptions.name: Concentrated loads
assumptions.value: valves, flanges, and other point loads are added to the per-hanger load separately

wind-shear-hub-height.formula: the power law v2 = v1 x (z2 / z1) raised to alpha; alpha derived from two measured levels is ln(v2/v1) / ln(z2/z1); the energy ratio is the speed ratio cubed.
wind-shear-hub-height.edition: The power-law wind shear relation by name, with the customary exponents 0.10 over water and smooth ground, 0.14 the open-country default, 0.20 over crops and scattered obstacles, and 0.25 to 0.40 over woodland and suburbs, and IEC 61400-12 named for the hub-height measurement this does not replace. An independent energy assessor governs a bankable estimate.
wind-shear-hub-height.freeAccess: Extrapolation between two heights on the user's own anemometer readings; no wind atlas or proprietary shear table is reproduced.
wind-shear-hub-height.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
wind-shear-hub-height.editionNote: The exponent is the whole calculation and it is site-specific. The 1/7 value of 0.14 that gets used as a default belongs to flat open country in neutral stability; over crops, brush, or trees the profile is much steeper and over water much flatter, so deriving it from two anemometer levels on the same mast is worth far more than any table and is the reason met masts carry multiple levels. The amplification is what makes it consequential: because power is cubic, an exponent wrong by a few hundredths produces a wind speed error of a few percent and an ENERGY error of roughly three times that, and on a twenty-year project that difference is the whole margin. Shear also varies through the day and the year -- nights are typically far more sheared than afternoons because the atmosphere stabilizes -- so a short measurement campaign taken in one season can mislead in both directions. Real profiles are not power laws at all over complex terrain or near forest canopies, where they can be displaced upward or even reversed, and extrapolating more than roughly twice the measurement height is not defensible.

assumptions.name: The exponent is measured, not assumed
assumptions.value: two levels on one mast beat any published table

assumptions.name: A speed error triples in energy
assumptions.value: because power goes as the cube of speed

assumptions.name: About twice the measurement height is the practical limit
assumptions.value: a rule of thumb for bankable energy assessment, not a standard figure -- screening atlases (NREL) extrapolate 10 m to 50 m with the 1/7 law

flow-hood-correction.formula: corrected flow = hood reading x correction factor; where a reference traverse is entered the factor is DERIVED as traverse / reading; the report total corrects by the same factor, and the difference is the systematic error the uncorrected report carried.
flow-hood-correction.edition: The balancing-hood correction as AABC and NEBB field practice states it, with the factor best established on the actual system by comparing hood readings against a duct traverse rather than taken from a table. It does not model the back pressure from the hood's own resistance, select a hood or adapter, or capture placement failures such as an unsealed hood or a linear slot without the right adapter.
flow-hood-correction.freeAccess: One multiplication and one ratio; no manufacturer table is reproduced.
flow-hood-correction.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
flow-hood-correction.editionNote: A hood is a resistance in series with the diffuser, and adding resistance to a system reduces the flow through it, so a hood commonly reads LOW -- but how much depends on the diffuser's available pressure, and the direction can run either way, so it is COMPUTED from the factor here rather than asserted. What matters more than the direction is that the error is SYSTEMATIC: it is the same sign on every reading, so it does not average out across a report and an uncorrected total misstates the whole system by the same proportion it misstates one outlet.

assumptions.name: The factor is not a property of the hood alone
assumptions.value: it depends on the diffuser and the system's available pressure
assumptions.source: a duct traverse on the same system

assumptions.name: Placement failures are not captured
assumptions.value: an unsealed hood or a missing slot adapter is larger than any factor

assumptions.name: It measures nothing
assumptions.value: this corrects a reading you took

coil-capacity-verification.formula: air sensible Q = 1.08 x CFM x dT; air total Q = 4.5 x CFM x dh on a wet coil; water Q = fluid factor x GPM x dT with 500 for water; the heat balance difference is the gap between the air side used and the water side, as a percentage of the water side, judged against an entered tolerance.
coil-capacity-verification.edition: The coil heat balance as ASHRAE and balancing practice writes it, where 1.08 is 0.075 lb/cu ft x 0.24 BTU/lb-degF x 60 min/h, 4.5 is 0.075 x 60, and 500 is 8.33 lb/gal x 60 x 1.0. The tolerance and the fluid factor are ENTERED (glycol-fluid-factor gives the factor for a propylene glycol loop). Sea-level standard air: it does not correct for altitude or non-standard density (air-density-correction gives the corrected 1.08 and 4.5 factors), derive enthalpy from dry-bulb and wet-bulb readings, assess instrument accuracy, or evaluate coil cleanliness, circuiting or approach.
coil-capacity-verification.freeAccess: Three constants and two temperature differences.
coil-capacity-verification.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
coil-capacity-verification.editionNote: Two independent measurements are the whole value of the exercise: agreement is strong evidence that both are right, and disagreement LOCALISES the problem. Air side high points at an overstated airflow or at air bypassing the coil; water side high usually means the flow measurement is wrong or the sensors are too close together for the delta. The sensible-versus-total distinction is the trap, because a sensible-only air side will fall short of a wet coil's water side for no reason but the method -- and correcting the method does NOT license calling any remaining disagreement acceptable, which is why the tolerance is entered and the verdict computed against it.

assumptions.name: Sea-level standard air
assumptions.value: 1.08 and 4.5 carry a 0.075 lb/cu ft density

assumptions.name: Enthalpy is entered, not derived
assumptions.value: it needs wet-bulb readings on both sides

assumptions.name: The water delta is the weak measurement
assumptions.value: a small delta with degree-accurate sensors carries large uncertainty

pipeline-potential-attenuation.formula: R_L = steel resistivity / steel area; R_G = coating resistance / surface per foot; alpha = sqrt(R_L / R_G); R_k = sqrt(R_L x R_G); shift at x = drain shift x e^(-alpha x).
pipeline-potential-attenuation.edition: The infinite-line attenuation relations. The pipeline's own close interval survey governs.
pipeline-potential-attenuation.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
pipeline-potential-attenuation.editionNote: A tenfold coating degradation raises the attenuation constant only by its square root, but the reach still falls by that factor. The far-end test stations show the coating's condition; the rectifier does not.

assumptions.name: Line
assumptions.value: infinite and uniformly coated; a finite line or a holiday changes it

assumptions.name: Steel resistivity
assumptions.value: entered; about 7.1 x 10^-6 ohm-in for line pipe
